result.summary: Metrics: turnaround time = completion time - arrival time; waiting time = turnaround time - burst time; response time = first run time - arrival time. Priority scheduling: runs the highest-priority process first. It gives the minimum average waiting time but needs a prediction of burst length and can starve long processes. Round Robin (RR): each process gets a fixed time quantum and then goes to the back of the ready queue. Shortest Job First (SJF): runs the process with the smallest next CPU burst. The CPU scheduler picks which process in the ready queue runs next.

key_terms.definition: If the quantum is very large, RR behaves like FCFS; if it is very small, context-switch overhead dominates.
key_terms.evidence: If the quantum is very large, RR behaves like FCFS; if it is very small, context-switch overhead dominates.

result.summary: Slow start begins with a small congestion window (cwnd) and roughly doubles it every round trip until it reaches the slow-start threshold (ssthresh); then congestion avoidance increases cwnd by about one segment per round trip. Sequence numbers label bytes so the receiver can reorder segments and detect loss; acknowledgements (ACKs) tell the sender what has been received. Flow control uses the receiver's advertised window (rwnd) so the sender does not overwhelm the receiver's buffer. When a packet loss is detected by a timeout, TCP sets ssthresh to half of cwnd and restarts slow start. Congestion control protects the network.
